name: mfoc
desc: Implementation of 'offline nested' attack by Nethemba
why: Implements the offline nested attack that cracks MIFARE Classic key material, a vivid look at how broken RFID card crypto actually falls.

brief.what_it_is: MFOC is a command-line tool that recovers authentication keys from MIFARE Classic RFID/NFC cards. You place one MIFARE Classic tag on the reader and run mfoc with options. It needs at least one key the tag already accepts, either its built-in default key or a custom key you pass on the command line, and it then recovers the other keys from the card. The README does not describe its output format.
brief.why_it_exists: The README frames MFOC as an open source implementation of the "offline nested" attack by Nethemba, applied to MIFARE Classic cards.
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the mechanism beyond naming the offline nested attack. It states the precondition: recovery only works if the tool already has one valid key for the target, either the hardcoded default or one supplied by the user.

commands_seen.context: Build step from source: generates the configure script (autotools).
Build step from source: configures the build.
Build step from source: compiles and installs mfoc system-wide, using sudo for the install.
Usage: prints the available command-line options. The README says to run this to see what options to pass.

brief.install_notes: Build from source with autoreconf -is, ./configure, then make and sudo make install. The README mentions no hardware beyond a MIFARE Classic tag, no accounts, and no runtime dependencies. The Homebrew formula supplies the mfoc executable. The README does not list the reader hardware or library requirements.
brief.standout: It is a focused, single-purpose tool for a well-known weakness in MIFARE Classic cards. It shows concretely how the card's crypto falls once one key is known.
brief.status: unknown. The README gives no release date, version, or changelog, and the fetched page showed no last-commit information. I did not check the repository's commit history or releases, so I cannot say whether it is maintained.
brief.caveats: Recovery only works if the target has a known key, either the hardcoded default or a custom one you supply; the README is explicit that MFOC cannot recover keys without one. It is for MIFARE Classic cards only. Build from source requires autotools (autoreconf). The README does not state a license. The README is brief, and the reader hardware and supported platforms are not documented.
quotes: MFOC is an open source implementation of "offline nested" attack by Nethemba.
This program allow to recover authentication keys from MIFARE Classic card.
MFOC is able to recover keys from target only if it have a known key: default one (hardcoded in MFOC) or custom one (user provided using command line).
